column3: NASB follows the critical text (“again a large crowd”) but names “Jesus” and “His disciples” from the Textus Receptus.
NASB rearranges the sentence and adds “to find enough” and “people.”
NASB renders “recline” as “sit down,” “set before” as “serve,” and “the crowd” as “the people.”
NASB renders the Hebrew-style oath “if a sign will be given” as “no sign will be given.”
NASB follows the critical text (“they had no bread”), adding “the fact that.”
NASB names “Jesus” (Textus Receptus) and follows the critical text without “still” before “hardened”; it renders “perceive” as “see.”
Close to the Greek; the Old Testament phrases are in capitals.
“Hand-baskets” is rendered “baskets.” The quotation marks in the NASB text here are misplaced.
NASB adds “I broke” and “large”; the quotation marks in the NASB text here are misplaced.
NASB follows the critical text (“he looked intently and was restored”).
NASB follows the critical text with “Do not even enter the village,” without the Textus Receptus “nor tell anyone in the village.”
NASB follows the critical text; “was questioning” is rendered “continued by questioning.”
